title: Database Architecture
relevance: SDE interviews probe whether candidates can separate DBMS data-organization levels from application deployment tiers and explain data independence.

phases.goal: Establish the ANSI/SPARC three-schema levels and what a schema is versus an instance.

must_hit.point: The three-schema architecture organises a database into three levels of abstraction whose purpose is data independence.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names external, conceptual, and internal levels and states the goal is insulating each level from changes beneath it.

must_hit.point: The external level has many external schemas (tailored user views); the conceptual level has a single conceptual schema (whole logical map); the internal level has the physical schema (on-disk storage, indexes, B-trees).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate distinguishes many views vs one logical schema vs physical storage structures.

must_hit.point: A schema is the description of structure fixed at design time; an instance is the data values that populate it at a given moment.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate contrasts structure (e.g. Student attributes) with the current populated data.

probes: What are the three levels in the ANSI/SPARC architecture, and what does each describe?

hints.1: Think about what different users see versus the whole logical design versus how bytes sit on disk.
hints.2: Map external → views, conceptual → tables/relationships/rules, internal → files/indexes/B-trees.
hints.3: Purpose is data independence: many external schemas, one conceptual schema, one physical schema below which the database sits on disk.

phases.goal: Explain logical and physical data independence and how each is achieved.

must_hit.point: Logical data independence means changing the conceptual schema without disturbing external schemas and applications; it is realised chiefly through views and is harder in practice.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate ties conceptual changes (add table, split relation) to shielding applications via views and notes it is the harder grade.

must_hit.point: Physical data independence means changing the physical schema without touching the conceptual schema—e.g. storage structure, underlying data structure, or adding/dropping an index.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists physical changes that should not require logical design or application changes.

probes: What is the difference between logical and physical data independence?

hints.1: One shields users/apps from logical redesign; the other shields the logical design from storage changes.
hints.2: Ask which level is changing: conceptual vs physical, and what stays stable above it.
hints.3: Logical: change conceptual schema, keep external schemas via views (harder). Physical: change storage/indexes/data structures, keep conceptual schema.

phases.goal: Contrast two-tier versus three-tier placement of software and why a middle tier helps.

must_hit.point: In two-tier architecture, clients talk directly to the database server—only clients and the database.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes direct client-to-DB connection with no middle application server.

must_hit.point: In three-tier architecture, presentation, application/business, and data layers are separated so clients talk to an application server that talks to the database, aiding scalability and keeping concerns from tangling.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names the three layers and states separation of UI, business logic, and storage plus scalability.

probes: How does a three-tier architecture differ from a two-tier one, and what does the extra tier buy you?

hints.1: Ask where the business logic lives—on the client path to the DB, or on a middle server.
hints.2: Sketch client → DB versus client → application server → data source.
hints.3: Three-tier: presentation, business, data; extra tier separates UI, logic, and storage and aids scalability.

phases.goal: Show how three-schema and three-tier relate in a real request path without conflating them.

must_hit.point: Three-schema is about how data is hidden and organised inside a DBMS; three-tier is about where software code runs; the entire three-schema stack lives inside the three-tier data tier.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate states the keypoint: organisation/independence vs deployment, with three-schema inside the data tier.

must_hit.point: On a request like View Profile, presentation hits the application tier, which queries the data tier; inside the DBMS the query uses an external view/API, maps via the conceptual schema, then reads bytes via the internal schema.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate walks request up/down the tiers and then through external → conceptual → internal inside the data tier.

probes: A candidate confuses three-schema with three-tier—how would you explain how they fit together on a View Profile request?

hints.1: One is DBMS abstraction levels; the other is where UI, logic, and DB processes run.
hints.2: Place the whole three-schema stack inside the data tier, then narrate one user action.
hints.3: Phone (presentation) → backend (application) → DB (data); inside DB: external view → conceptual tables → internal on-disk bytes.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Two-tier has clients talk directly to the database; three-tier inserts an application/business layer between presentation and data so UI, business logic, and storage stay separated, which aids scalability and avoids tangled concerns.

Three-schema (ANSI/SPARC) organises data inside a DBMS for data independence (external/conceptual/internal); three-tier is a deployment split of presentation, application, and data. The whole three-schema architecture sits inside the three-tier data tier.

gotchas.trap: Treating three-schema and three-tier as the same three-layer stack because both say three.
gotchas.correction: They describe different things: three-schema is DBMS data organisation and independence; three-tier is where code runs. Hold them by nesting the entire three-schema stack inside the three-tier data tier.

gotchas.trap: Assuming physical storage changes (indexes, B-trees, file layout) must force application or conceptual redesign.
gotchas.correction: Physical data independence means changing the physical schema—storage structure, data structures, indexes—should not require changing the conceptual schema or applications.

gotchas.trap: Assuming logical redesign (add table, split relation) always breaks every user-facing app with no mitigation.
gotchas.correction: Logical data independence aims to change the conceptual schema without disturbing external schemas, realised chiefly through views—though it is harder to achieve in practice.
